newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysian firm in retender for U.S. corn/soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian firm in retender for U.S. corn/soybeans.

text.p: A Malaysian company will retender later on Thursday for a combined shipment of 50,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and soybeans, traders said on Thursday.
"Soon Soon (Sdn Bhd) passed on a tender for the shipment recently, but they're holding a retender later this afternoon," a dealer in a European commodity house said.
"That tender by Soon Soon is the only thing on the horizon right now if you're talking of regional business. There's nothing else," a trader in a U.S. commodity house said.
The delivery date of the shipment is from January 26 to February 5, traders said.
One dealer said Soon Soon passed on its earlier tender on the expectation that prices in the U.S. will ease.
"I don't know if they'll get a different price now. I think it's even gone up a bit," the dealer said.

The price of U.S. corn coming into Southeast Asia was quoted by regional dealers at around US$149-$150 a tonne C&F on board a Panamax vessel for February/April shipment against $147-$149 a tonne C&F last week for January/February shipment.
U.S. soybeans were priced around $298-$299 a tonne C&F for February/April on board a Panamax against the previous week's $298-$300 a tonne C&F for January/February, dealers said.
Plans by buyers in Indonesia and Malaysia, however, to purchase about 10,000 to 20,000 tonnes each of Indian-origin soymeal for nearby shipment fell through after failure to reach agreement on price.

"Everybody in the buying side was looking at a price of US$290 (a tonne C&F), but nobody wanted to do this. We are not a charity organisation," a senior dealer for another European trading house said. "They eventually backed out."
A U.S. trader said the Malaysians and Indonesians decided against the purchase "when they saw prices for soymeal begin to creep up. That's when the proposed deal fell through."

The price of Indian soymeal going into the region was quoted at around $303-$307 a tonne C&F on board a Tweendecker for nearby shipment, up from a quote last week of $295-$300 a tonne C&F, traders said.
"They just couldn't bridge their differences on the price," a trader said.
Another dealer said buyers in both countries could afford to sit back a few more weeks since "they still have some coverage. It's a no-rush situation for them."

News of storms which devastated 200,000 hectares in Argentina's southern wheat belt did not have an impact in the market since most of the wheat in the region is bought either from the United States or even Australia, the traders said.
With regional business slowing down ahead of the Christmas and New Year holiday period, most dealers were looking at taking a break themselves.
"The market is so dead and quiet I'm going on a vacation by the end of the week," a dealer in a European trading house said.
A trader for a U.S. commodity firm said they will just make sure ships they have contracted to deliver cargo over the next few days make it on time to their ports of destination.
"There's nothing out there," the trader said. "Last year, the buying was much better."
